rail_guard.text: Nottingham Station. Trains for every station you have visited. Please stand clear of the platform edge, the lace curtains and the large goose.

then.text: Sun's out over the Lace Market. Lovely light through a lace curtain, that. Pretty patterns on the floor.
Warehouse windows glowing at dusk. You can picture the lace frames clattering away inside.

not_lace.text: Nottingham lace was machine-made on frames of cast iron, a bit like a very precise loom. The lace curtains in your gran's front window were probably made here.
The Lace Market warehouses have a big sign inside saying 'Gents' and a small sign saying 'Please do not iron the exhibits'.

then.text: Raining up top? Down in the caves it's dry as a biscuit. Nottingham always did think ahead.
Fog on the streets, and the caves stay exactly the same. Cool, quiet and full of old secrets.

not_caver.text: There's a city under the city. Eight hundred caves, hand-cut with pick and chisel in the soft stone. Tanners, brewers, bakers, hiders. Nottingham likes to keep something in reserve.
In the war, the caves were air raid shelters. Now they're museums and wine cellars. Not at the same time.

not_footie.text: Nottingham Forest won the European Cup. Twice. In a row. 1979 and 1980. We bring it up whenever we are, to be fair, losing at something else.
Brian Clough managed them. He once said, 'I wouldn't say I was the best manager in the business, but I was in the top one.' I'm proud, and also dubious.

then.text: Drizzle, duck? Goose Fair's had worse. Pull your hood up and get a bag of mushy peas, it'll warm you through.
The fair lights look best at dusk, duck. Everything's sparkly and the waltzers are already spinning.

not_goose.text: Goose Fair started as a medieval market where people sold geese. Now it sells mushy peas and a ride that goes upside down. The geese went home, but the name stayed.
A bag of brandy snap, a toffee apple and a whirl on the waltzers. That's a Nottingham October. Everything else is bunting.

then.text: Raining, so Brenda's got her mudguards on. She doesn't like getting her chain wet. Fair enough.
Wind's against me all the way up to the Castle. Brenda says we're training. Brenda fibs.
Morning ride before work. Empty streets, birds singing, and Brenda's bell waking up half of Sneinton.

not_cyclist.text: Raleigh bicycles started here in 1887, and soon they made hundreds of thousands a year. It was a Nottingham invention. I'm not saying the bike was a Nottingham invention. I'm saying the best ones were.
My bike's called Brenda. She's got a bell like a church.

nottingham_night_nurse.text: Off to the Queen's Medical Centre for the night shift, duck. It's that big, you need a map to find the canteen.
Nights are quiet on the streets but never on the wards. Mind how you go, and don't trip over any geese.
Flask of tea, a sandwich and a slice of Bramley apple pie. Proper night shift supplies, that.

nottingham_lamplighter.text: Evening! Somebody's got to light the way past the Castle. Robin Hood used arrows. I use a pole.
Quiet streets, warm lamps, and a hedgehog doing his rounds on Old Market Square. Lovely night for it.
